title: POC weekly sync - model selection and pinning
summary: Weekly POC sync to review pilot results across candidate models, decide final model selection and exact version pinning for the next phase. Discussed regressions on a small prompt set, latency/cost tradeoffs, and agreed on a pinned config + rollback strategy. Action items assigned for benchmarks, pricing, and security docs.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-02-23 14:00 PST | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Ava Martinez, Samir Rao (Redwood) — Maya Brooks, Ethan Wright, Priya Menon (Orion Retail)

[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — let's kick off. Quick roll call — say hi?
[00:06] Maya Brooks: Hi, Maya here.
[00:08] Ethan Wright: Ethan, infra.
[00:09] Priya Menon: Priya, product.
[00:11] Samir Rao: Samir from Redwood SE.
[00:13] Ava Martinez: Great. Agenda — results from last week's benchmark, model selection, pinning strategy, fallback/rollback plan, next steps.

[01:02] Priya Menon: Quick context — our prime metric is user-facing latency under 600ms p50 for short chats, and accuracy on our 120 prompt evaluation suite. Cost is second but still important.
[01:18] Ethan Wright: Also infra constraint — we want VPC-only traffic and KMS keys for encryption, so private connector will be used in Dedicated trial.

[03:05] Samir Rao: On the benchmark side we ran three candidate model variants — redwood-7b-qlora-v1 (fp16), redwood-7b-qlora-v2 (int8), and a smaller redwood-3b-quant. Results: v2 gives ~20% lower token cost and 30% lower p50 latency vs v1 in our infra, but we saw a minor regression on recall for multi-step prompts in the evaluation set.
[03:25] Maya Brooks: Can you clarify "minor"? We had 6 prompts drop from 0.82 -> 0.73 F1-ish. That's noticeable for the use case.
[03:33] Samir Rao: Yeah that's accurate, on those few multi-step extraction tasks v2 sometimes hallucinates a step. We suspect quantization coupled with the prompt window causing some attention degradation; though for most conversational prompts it's fine.

[06:10] Ava Martinez: Okay, so tradeoff: v2 gives cost and latency benefits but slight quality hit on a narrow subset. Option A: pin to v1 for safety; Option B: pin to v2 and set up narrow fallback to v1 for detected multi-step triggers; Option C: hybrid routing by route or by prompt classifier.

[07:05] Priya Menon: Hybrid sounds appealing but adds infra complexity. Do we have existing classifier for detecting those multi-step prompts?
[07:12] Samir Rao: Not out-of-the-box; we can provide a simple n-gram/pattern classifier or a tiny transformer that flags those cases. Runtime overhead is small — ~15ms — but adds an additional inference call unless run locally.

[09:00] Ethan Wright: For Dedicated we could host the classifier in your VPC along side the runtime to avoid extra egress. But that needs support for our private network. Does Redwood support private canaries?
[09:11] Ava Martinez: Yes — Dedicated supports private routing via the private control plane; we can push a small model for prompt classification into the same pool. We'll include config examples.

[11:45] Maya Brooks: Another question — pinning behavior. If we pin to v2 and later see quality degrade we want an emergency rollback. What's the recommended rollback/fallback policy?
[11:53] Samir Rao: We recommend: pin the route to an exact model version (e.g., redwood-7b-qlora-v2-20270218), enable a canary for 5% traffic to the new version for 48 hours, automated quality checks on your eval set (we can run a webhook that fails the canary if metrics drop), and a pre-configured rollback to v1. Then set a fallback policy: if latency or error rate exceeds SLO, route to v1 or the smaller quant model.

[14:30] Priya Menon: How quickly can rollback happen?
[14:34] Samir Rao: Immediately — it's a control plane switch, typically sub-minute for routing to change, token streams in-progress will finish on the old path but new requests go to fallback. We'll document TTLs and cache invalidation specifics.

[16:20] Maya Brooks: About observability — we need token-level cost, per-route latency, and per-prompt quality traces tied to prompt IDs. Are those available in Redwood console?
[16:30] Ava Martinez: Yes — Console provides per-route token and latency breakdowns, and you can attach prompt IDs so exports include prompt->response->metric lines. We'll show an example export.

[18:55] Ethan Wright: Security — we need SOC2, ISO certs, KMS integration and audit logs for model access. Any blockers for Dedicated?
[19:05] Samir Rao: No blockers. Dedicated includes audit logs and supports customer KMS via our connector; for on-prem we support HSM integrations. We'll share the security packet and SOC2 report.

[21:40] Priya Menon: Back to metrics — Samir, can you summarize exact numbers from this week's run for p50/p95 and token cost?
[21:49] Samir Rao: Sure: redwood-7b-qlora-v1: p50 520ms, p95 990ms, est token cost $0.012/token (normalized); v2: p50 370ms, p95 720ms, est token cost $0.009/token; 3b-quant: p50 290ms but lower quality on longer prompts, cost $0.006/token.

[24:10] Maya Brooks: Based on that, leaning to v2 + fallback to v1 for those 6 problematic prompts. But we want to run an extended eval overnight using our 1,200 prompt set to quantify frequency.
[24:22] Priya Menon: ETA — we can run it tonight and share results tomorrow EOD.

[26:00] Ava Martinez: Technical note — for pinning exact versions we'll provide config snippets you can apply to your route: model: redwood-7b-qlora-v2@20270218, fallback: redwood-7b-qlora-v1@20270112, canary: 5% for 48h. Also include automatic rollback webhook.

[28:45] Ethan Wright: One gotcha — what about the KV cache / prefix caching when routing between models? If we fallback mid-session will KV cache compatibility break?
[28:56] Samir Rao: Good call. KV cache formats are compatible across these variants, but if you switch to a different architecture (e.g., 3b-quant vs 7b) we recommend dropping the session cache. We'll add a header flag to force cache flush on fallback for those routes.

[31:12] Priya Menon: Can we get a short playbook for incidents — who to page and SLA expectations?
[31:20] Ava Martinez: Yes — we'll include on-call contacts for Dedicated trial, SLA targets (99.9% up, latency SLOs) and escalation matrix.

[33:05] Maya Brooks: Any impact to data residency? We need EU-only for a subset of traffic.
[33:12] Samir Rao: We support region routing — you can pin region in the routing policy. For Dedicated we'll ensure the pool is in your EU region and data never leaves.

[35:00] Priya Menon: Ok let's do a decision moment — do we want to pin to v2 with fallback to v1 and run the extended eval tonight? Maya: yay or nay?
[35:10] Maya Brooks: Vote yes, with fallback to v1 and a canary of 5% for 48 hours.
[35:17] Ethan Wright: Agree.
[35:19] Priya Menon: Agree.

[36:00] Ava Martinez: Recap — pin to redwood-7b-qlora-v2@20270218, fallback to redwood-7b-qlora-v1@20270112, canary 5% 48h, run Orion's 1,200 prompt eval tonight, Redwood to share pricing and security packet and pinned config. We'll also provide a small prompt-classifier example to detect multi-step prompts and a config for cache flush on fallback.

[38:10] Samir Rao: Quick note — we'll attach the raw benchmark spreadsheet and a notebook to reproduce. Also include sample autoscaling policies to keep p95 under 1s.

[40:45] Priya Menon: Anything else?
[41:00] Maya Brooks: No, thanks. Good sync.
[41:10] Ava Martinez: Thanks all — we'll follow up with notes and action items.

[44:30] Meeting ends.
